summary: Trump retains executive authority while Democrats prepare to take control of Congress in January. Stephen Miller reportedly began as chief of staff on November 9, giving him more ability to manage White House staff and proposals reaching Trump; Susie Wiles’s political responsibilities remain unclear. Representative Thomas Massie has moved his Hegseth impeachment effort onto the House floor, while Trump defends his defense secretary. That dispute creates pressure over the war and the president’s personnel choices without establishing a vote result or removal. The Supreme Court has temporarily lifted the injunction blocking Big Bend border-wall construction, a specific legal opening rather than proof of completed building or broader enforcement success. Qatar’s prime minister reportedly met Trump and Vice President JD Vance, but an Iran settlement remains unverified. Nvidia’s inquiry, Israel’s government formation and Minneapolis’s November 12 data-center zoning decision remain open. Today’s Republican leadership results, outstanding election calls, Russia-Ukraine talks and major unresolved court proceedings require follow-up. Tariffs, the Fed, Epstein oversight and Venezuela retain carried findings and incomplete fresh coverage. All eight estimates hold at November 9 levels under the weekly cadence.
